proposed.explanation:
You need approximately 30,000 EGP within 6 months, but you currently hold only 5,000 EGP in cash. You must therefore liquidate part of your COMI position. Selling 196 shares at 128 EGP yields 25,088 EGP, bringing your cash to 30,088 EGP and meeting your liquidity requirement.

COMI (a large Egyptian bank) shows strong fundamental momentum: net profit rose from 55,256,732,000 EGP in FY2024 to 82,258,815,000 EGP in FY2025 (≈49 % growth), and basic EPS increased from 14.72 to 18.25 EGP. At the current price of 128 EGP the implied P/E is roughly 7×, which is not expensive for a bank growing at this rate. The balance sheet is large (due to customers ≈ 1.11 trillion EGP; total equity and retained profit ≈ 231.5 billion EGP), suggesting a systemically important institution.

However, your stated profile—capital preservation, low loss tolerance, a hard 30,000 EGP cash need within six months, and a 1–3-year horizon—makes it imprudent to keep the entire position in a single equity. Selling 196 shares (about 19.6 % of your holding) addresses the immediate cash gap while leaving you with 804 shares (≈102,912 EGP) still exposed to the bank's earnings growth. You do not need to sell more than this to meet the stated liquidity need, and the evidence does not indicate any deterioration that would justify a larger reduction.

Risks and uncertainties: (1) No dividend data is provided in the evidence, so I cannot confirm whether COMI pays a regular income stream that would suit your 'draw income' goal. (2) A single-stock portfolio, even after this sale, remains concentrated; if you can access other low-risk instruments (e.g., government bonds, money-market funds) in the future, diversifying further would reduce risk. (3) Bank earnings are sensitive to interest-rate and credit-cycle shifts; the strong FY2025 results do not guarantee the same pace going forward. (4) This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.

claims.statement: COMI net interest income for the year ended 31 Dec 2025 was 107,699,631 thousand EGP (107,699,631,000 EGP), up from 91,064,222 thousand EGP (91,064,222,000 EGP) in FY2024.

COMI net profit for the year ended 31 Dec 2025 was 82,258,815 thousand EGP (82,258,815,000 EGP), up from 55,256,732 thousand EGP (55,256,732,000 EGP) in FY2024, representing approximately 49 % year-on-year growth.
COMI basic earnings per share for FY2025 was 18.25 EGP, up from 14.72 EGP in FY2024 (≈24 % growth). At the current share price of 128 EGP this implies a P/E of roughly 7.0×.
COMI's due-to-customers (deposits) at 31 Dec 2025 was 1,110,395,693 thousand EGP (≈1.11 trillion EGP), indicating a large, systemically important bank.
COMI's total equity and net profit for the year at 31 Dec 2025 was 231,486,342 thousand EGP (≈231.5 billion EGP), up from 152,636,277 thousand EGP in FY2024.

limitations: No dividend or payout-ratio data is provided in the evidence, so I cannot assess whether COMI generates a reliable income stream for your retirement drawdown goal.
The evidence covers only FY2025 and FY2024 consolidated condensed figures; there is no quarterly trend, no forward guidance, and no information on credit-quality migration or NPL ratios.

The EPS figures are reported under a table whose unit line reads 'EGP thousands'; I have interpreted them as per-share EGP (18.25 and 14.72) consistent with standard reporting practice, but if the unit were applied literally the numbers would be 18,250 and 14,720 EGP, which would be inconsistent with the 128 EGP share price. This interpretation does not change the recommendation, which is driven by the liquidity need rather than the valuation.
No information is provided on COMI's dividend history, share buybacks, or any upcoming corporate actions that could affect the share price or income.
